questions.q: As we go from species to kingdom in a taxonomic hierarchy, the number of common characteristics
questions.solution: Lower taxa share more common characteristics as compared to higher taxa. So, as we go from species to kingdom in a taxonomic hierarchy, the number of common characteristics decreases. as we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics goes on decreasing. Lower the taxa, more are the characteristics that the members within the taxon share. Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining the relationship to other taxa at the same level. Hence, the problem of classification becomes more complex.

options: Identification and study of organ systems of plants and animal
Identification and preservation of plants and animals
Diversity of kinds of organisms and their relationship

questions.solution: Systematics is the diversity of different kinds of organisms and their relationship. Human beings were, since long, not only interested in knowing more about different kinds of organisms and their diversities, but also the relationships among them. This branch of study was referred to as systematics. The word systematics is derived from the Latin word ‘systema’ which means systematic arrangement of organisms. Linnaeus used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication. The scope of systematics was later enlarged to include identification, nomenclature and classification. Systematics takes into account evolutionary relationships between organisms.

questions.q: Genus represents
options: A collection of plants or animals
A group of closely related species of plants or animals
questions.solution: Genus is a group of closely related species of animals or plants. Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera. We can say that genera are aggregates of closely related species. For example, potato and brinjal are two different species but both belong to the genus Solanum. Lion (Panthera leo), leopard (P. pardus) and tiger (P. tigris) with several common features, are all species of the genus Panthera. This genus differs from another genus Felis which includes cats.

questions.q: How are genera defined in taxonomy?
questions.solution: Genera are defined as groups of related species with more characters in common compared to species of other genera, based on distinct morphological differences. Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera. We can say that genera are aggregates of closely related species. For example, potato and brinjal are two different species but both belong to the genus Solanum. Lion (Panthera leo), leopard (P. pardus) and tiger (P. tigris) with several common features, are all species of the genus Panthera. This genus differs from another genus Felis which includes cats.
